BadRequest.description: The request was refused. When it failed validation, `errors` lists each problem (`type`, `loc`, `msg`) and `detail` joins them; other refusals (a rule of the route, a bad `Content-Length`, HTTPS required) have `detail` and may add `reason`, `field` or other keys. This app answers **400** for a validation error, never 422.

BearerUnauthorized.description: No token, or a token that does not work here: unknown, revoked, expired, of the other family, without the scope, or the instance switch for this family is off. Every case is the same generic answer.

Conflict.description: The change clashes with what is stored or with a server rule: a name taken, the last admin, a setting fixed by the server's environment, a consent the person has not given yet, a list that is full.

Error.description: Any other error. Every error answer has the `Problem` shape: a `detail` sentence, and possibly more keys. Treat an unlisted status as an error with this body.

Forbidden.description: Refused. On `/api`: an unsafe request without the `X-Requested-With: kidney-health` header or from another site; a route for admins (`Admins only`); the password must be entered again (`reauth_required`) or changed first (`password_change_required`). On `/mcp` and `/push/v1/body`: a foreign `Origin` header.

Allow.description: The one method the route offers: `POST`.

NotFound.description: The record does not exist or is not the signed-in person's (the two look the same), or the feature is switched off on this server (the AI routes while the AI is off, `/mcp` while assistant access is off).

PayloadTooLarge.description: The request body is larger than this route allows (`MAX_BODY_BYTES` or the route's own limit).

TooManyRequests.description: Too many requests (a rate limit, a sign-in throttle, or a quota). Wait `Retry-After` seconds.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

Unauthorized.description: Not signed in (`Sign in required`): there is no valid session cookie. (Sign-in itself answers this for a wrong name or password.)

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The body is not the type the route reads (JSON, `image/jpeg`, a recording, `export.json`); `detail` names it.

AppliedRule.description: One rule behind the suggestion ("Why this number?"): source, grade and whether part of it is the project's opinion.

code.description: A machine-readable code for a refusal that has one (the out-of-scope refusals of suggested targets).

retry_after.description: Seconds to wait (429); the `Retry-After` header says the same.

TokenCreate.description:
``POST /api/me/tokens``. Unknown fields are refused, so a scope cannot be sent by name: ``can_log`` is the one
way to ask for ``assistant:log`` (it saves food and recipes) and ``can_prefs`` the one way to ask for ``assistant:prefs``
(it remembers tastes: likes and dislikes); ``assistant:read`` is always included, and neither choice gives the other.
``family`` is ``assistant`` (default, so the Assistant access screen works unchanged) or ``device`` (a phone shortcut's
token, whose one scope, ``body:write``, is not a choice: ``can_log`` and ``can_prefs`` are refused for it).
TokenCreate.title: TokenCreate

ValidationProblem.description: The 400 answer. `detail` joins the problems into one sentence (`field: message; field: message`); `errors` lists each one when the request failed validation and is absent for the other 400s (a rule of the route, not of the shape). The value the person sent is never echoed back.

loc.description: Where: `body`, `query` or `path`, then the field names and list positions.

ValidationProblem.title: ValidationProblem

WeightAlarmCheck.description: What the person's weight-gain alarm says about the latest weight (note 10 §4.4).
WeightAlarmCheck.title: WeightAlarmCheck

WeightCreate.description:
``POST /api/body/weights`` and ``PUT /api/body/weights/{id}``: one weighing, in kilograms (the unit the person sees
and types is display and entry only).
WeightCreate.title: WeightCreate

assistantToken.description: An assistant access token (`Authorization: Bearer kha_...`), made in Settings, Assistant access, with the scope `assistant:read` and optionally `assistant:log`. It works only at `/mcp`, and only while the instance switch `assistant.enabled` is on. No cookie is read there, and the cookie checks of `/api` do not apply.

deviceToken.description: A device token (`Authorization: Bearer khd_...`), made in Settings, Phone shortcuts, with the one scope `body:write`. It works only at `POST /push/v1/body`, only while the instance switch `push.enabled` is on, and it can add weights and blood pressure readings and read nothing. No cookie is read there.

session.description:
The signed-in person's session cookie: `__Host-kh_session` when the server is reached over HTTPS, `kh_session` over plain HTTP (each name is read only on its own scheme; this scheme lists the plain name because OpenAPI allows one). `POST /api/auth/login` sets it (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax; 30 days at most, 14 days idle) and `POST /api/auth/logout` ends it. With `AUTH_MODE=proxy` the identity comes from the trusted proxy's header instead, and with `AUTH_MODE=none` nobody signs in.

**Every unsafe request (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) to `/api` must also send the header `X-Requested-With: kidney-health`**, and an `Origin` it sends must be the server's own; without the header the answer is 403. A request that carries only a bearer token (either kind) is anonymous on `/api`: a token is never a sign-in here.
session.name: kh_session

info.description:
Self-hosted food log with renal-diet and type 1 diabetes nutrient warnings, meal planning and period summaries.

This document is checked in as `docs/api/openapi.json`. `info.version` is the app's version; `info.x-api-version` is the API version, an integer that is raised only for a breaking change. Every error answer is `{"detail": string, ...}`; request validation is **400** with `errors`, never 422. Sign in with `POST /api/auth/login` (a cookie, see the `session` scheme); `/mcp` and `/push/v1/body` take bearer tokens.
info.title: Kidney Health Food Log

post.description: Test connection (R4): models, structured mode, vision, and the Hermes tool check (20 per hour).

get.description: Counts only (requests and tokens per person and provider); admins never see AI content (R9).

Test transcription: one second of silence through the same transport and address rules. It needs AI on and
``STT_BASE_URL``; the answer's text is neither returned nor kept (a speech model may "hear" words in silence),
only whether the server answered a transcription.
A single-use invite link (shown once). The token travels in the URL fragment.

get.description: Request counts per person, provider and key scope (counts only, nothing about what was looked up).

post.description:
Local mode: a ``pending_setup`` account plus a one-time link where the person sets a password.
Proxy mode: pre-create the identity the proxy will send (no link).

delete.description: Void the account's open reset or account-setup link (404 when there is none).

post.description: A 24-hour, single-use link to set a new password (also unlocks a locked account).

End every active token of the person at once, assistant and device tokens alike (reason ``admin``); they can make
new ones. Works while the switches are off too. An unknown id is 404; a person with no active token gets
``{"revoked": 0}``.

delete.description: "Delete my AI history" (R9 step 5), with the answers kept for reuse. Usage counts stay (they hold no content).

get.description: The person's own AI activity: what was sent, what came back, what the rules decided (R9 step 5).

post.description:
One message of the Ask conversation: the rules answer a low or an emergency without the model; otherwise the
model looks up the app's own numbers with its read-only tools and its answer is checked in code before it is shown.

Agree to send data to a provider that now serves a feature of this purpose (``text``: meal ideas and
describe-a-meal, which may be routed to different providers; ``photos``; ``chat``), R9 step 3. ``voice`` is not
routed: the recording goes to the transcription server (``STT_BASE_URL``), and the consent rides with Ask, keyed to
the AI provider that serves Ask now (``chat``), so it follows Ask if Ask is moved to another provider.
AI ideas, order, swap picks or plan picks for one meal, checked by the rules (R3, note 06 §4.13).
"2 eggs, toast with butter": phrases with search terms; the person picks each match (R3).

Read the printed results of a lab report photo: ``{rows, dropped, provider, ...}`` of proposed rows (never saved).

Order, as for the label route: switches and the local AI (503) → headers (415/413) → consent for ``labs`` (409) → the
person's and a server AI slot (429) → only then the body (408), checked and rewritten like every photo.

get.description: What the person's AI buttons can do now: per feature where it runs (``routes``), consent, quota, photo features.

post.description:
One recording (the request body, ``audio/webm``, ``audio/ogg``, ``audio/mp4`` or ``audio/wav``) → ``{"text": ...}``.

``seconds`` is the page's own measure of the length, used only for the activity row's coarse length bucket.

Sign in. Database work runs in worker threads; the two waits (a slot of the instance-wide budget,
then a hashing slot, up to 5 s each) are awaited on the event loop, so a flood of sign-ins holds no
worker thread and every other route keeps answering.

Whose account a reset or account-setup link is for, so the page can show the username: when an
admin created the account, the person holding the link has never seen it. It tells the holder
nothing the link does not already give them (it can set the password and sign in).

400.description: Not a product barcode: reason check_digit | format | restricted | isbn | issn | coupon | reserved

404.description: Not found (or found without nutrition facts: name is set)

429.description: Lookup limits (per person, or the server-wide Open Food Facts budget); see Retry-After

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

502.description: A food database could not be reached or answered wrongly

503.description: No lookup source is switched on or usable for this person

get.description:
The whole builtin list in one answer, for a device's offline food search (note 02 §6 item 9, R5).
``If-None-Match`` with the last ``ETag`` → 304 without a body, so a device asks every day for a few bytes and
downloads the list again only when it changed. ``/api`` answers stay ``Cache-Control: no-store``: the device
keeps the list and its ETag itself (js/offline.js).

304.description: The list has not changed since the ETag sent

post.description:
Fetch a FoodData Central record into the one shared ``usda`` row for that ``fdc_id`` and link
it to the caller (another person's import of the same food is reused, never exposed).

delete.description:
Own custom food: hidden when your entries or saved meals use it, else deleted. Shared food:
only your link is removed (other people keep theirs, §9 N5 (2)).

post.description:
An editable custom copy. It keeps the barcode (so the next scan finds the copy first), the
ingredient list and the attribution of the data it came from (ODbL needs it); the quality notes
belong to the provider's data and are not copied.

get.description:
The person's low-treatment foods at the amount that treats a low, lowest potassium first, with
the "Treating a low" card (§4.6). Never filtered by a budget, never switched off, never sent to AI.
End-of-day insights (§4.8) from eaten entries; planned ones are counted in ``planned_excluded``.
Period insights (§4.8): default the 7 days ending yesterday; at most 92 days.

The signals the ranking learned from this person's log, each with a plain reason (note 09 §4.4): foods eaten
often, foods usually eaten in one meal, usual meals, foods planned again and again but not eaten. Computed on the
spot by the same rules the ranking uses, never stored; empty with "Learn from my log" off.
What fits now (§4.5): foods, saved and usual meals that fit ``meal`` on ``date``.

delete.description: Suggest this food again. 404 when it is not on the person's "Not for me" list (another preference stays).

put.description:
Never suggest this food again (it stays searchable and loggable); replaces another preference on the food.
404 for a food the person cannot use; 409 at the limit of 500.

post.description:
Plan the rest of the day (§4.7). Computes only; "Use this plan" sends ``apply.entries`` to
``POST /api/log/batch``.

get.description: The person's food preferences by name, their food-group choices and the "Learn from my log" switch.

delete.description: Forget what was said about this food. 404 when there is nothing.

put.description:
Say ``like``, ``less`` (less often), ``not_for_me`` or ``neutral`` (stop using what was learned) about one food,
replacing what was there. ``source`` is ``ask`` for a change the Ask chat proposed and the person confirmed. 404
for a food the person cannot use; 409 at the limits.

get.description: Every number of the engine, its version and the handbook pages it links to (for the docs page).

Swap ideas (§4.6) for a food and amount before saving (``food_id`` + ``servings`` or ``grams``,
with ``date`` and ``meal``) or for a saved entry (``entry_id``). ``purpose=hypo`` (the default for a
low-treatment food, as when logging) asks only for other low treatments at the full amount;
``purpose=none`` treats it as food.
Where the app's Learn links go, and the pages warnings, alerts and notes link to.

200.description: Repeat of a client_id: the entry already created

post.description:
Add 1–40 entries in one transaction ("Use this plan", the offline outbox; note 06 §4.10).

Each item is validated exactly as ``POST /api/log`` (body rules, then the food must be visible).
All or nothing: the first failing item (``entries[i]: …``) rolls the whole batch back. Items whose
``client_id`` the person already used are not added again; their result is ``existing``. 201 when
at least one entry was created, 200 when every item already existed.

200.description: Every item was a repeat of its client_id

post.description:
Copy a day's entries onto another date (snapshot recomputed from the current foods).

Entries entered by weight keep their grams (servings follow the food's current
serving size); all others keep their servings. Notes are copied.
Set every planned entry of the day (or of one meal) to ``eaten``.

Create a custom food from manually entered nutrients, then log it. A repeated ``client_id``
answers 200 with the entry already created and creates no second food.

200.description: Repeat of a client_id: the entry already created

get.description:
Period summary of *eaten* entries: averages per logged day vs targets, days over,
the same-length previous period and, for hemodialysis, the current interdialytic interval.

Default: the 7 days ending today. Giving only one bound fills the other for a 7-day period.

The key is write-only: it is sealed to this row and shown as ``{set, last4}`` only.

Needs the current password (OWASP); signs out every other device and renews this session.

One family's tokens (``?family=assistant`` by default, or ``device``). The list works while the family's switch is
off too, so a person can still see and revoke their tokens.

post.description:
A new token, in this answer only (``token``); needs a recent password, like saving a key. ``family`` is
``assistant`` (default) or ``device``. An assistant token is read-only unless ``can_log`` (default false) also lets it
save food and recipes (``assistant:log``) and ``can_prefs`` (default false) lets it remember tastes (``assistant:prefs``).
A device token's scopes are always exactly ``["body:write"]``: the request cannot choose them (``can_log`` and
``can_prefs`` are refused for it).

Delete every weight and blood pressure reading this person's device token sent (rows whose ``api_token_id`` is the token) and
nothing else: a row the person typed, imported, or edited afterwards (an edit makes it theirs) stays. The token must be one of
the person's own **device** tokens; any other id (another person's, an assistant token, one already purged) is a 404. Works for a
revoked or expired token that is still in the list. Audited as ``body.token_rows_deleted`` with the counts. Answers
``{"deleted": {"weights": n, "readings": n}}``.

Save that day's entries of one meal (eaten and planned) as a template for that meal slot

``targets`` is merged key by key: keys that are sent overwrite (``null`` means
"not tracked"), keys that are not sent keep their stored value. ``dialysis_days``
replaces the whole list (``null`` or ``[]`` clears it) and is stored for any
``dialysis`` value; only the hemodialysis summary uses it.
